chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted: "He is worthy of being feared and worthy of granting forgiveness," he said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "I am the most entitled to be feared, provided My servant does not associate anything with Me, and I am the most entitled, if My servant does not associate anything with Me, to admit him into Paradise."
And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has sworn by His might and majesty that He will never punish the people of His monotheism with the Fire."

key_terms.تَوْحِيدِهِ: His monotheism (pure belief in One God)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is 'worthy of being feared' and 'worthy of granting forgiveness' according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to elucidate the grammatical structure of the verse, interpreting 'Ahl al-Taqwa' and 'Ahl al-Maghfirah' as divine attributes indicating Allah's worthiness of being feared and forgiving. It highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Tawhid* (monotheism) as the decisive criterion for salvation, reinforced by a specific divine oath (*Qasam*) that believers free from *Shirk* (associating partners with Allah) are guaranteed exemption from Hellfire.
